preserve: Every vehicle, tree, and spectator is live output from the public library pipeline under one selected MediumId.
Oil remains the default medium; Follow and Full course remain explicit camera modes that preserve race state.
Keyboard, touch, standard gamepad, visible focus, reduced-motion, and renderer recovery remain first-class behavior.
change: Make the live race consume the viewport and move telemetry into terse angular overlays.
Replace the broad loop with a technical course, visible collision fixtures, scenery, grandstand, and character crowd.
Make speed, slip angle, drift chain, impact, and recovery legible as game events rather than background state.
discard: The header-plus-sidebar dashboard composition and its large settings form.
The oval-looking course, hidden centre-line recovery force, slow scalar handling, and quiet spreadsheet-like running order.
The previous v1 implementation renders and comparison boards as active visual authority.

productTruth.user: A keyboard, touch, or standard-gamepad player seeking a short, immediately legible, exaggerated arcade drift race in Doodle 3D.
productTruth.primaryTask: Launch into a three-lap technical race, drift through visible corners and barriers, read speed and race position at a glance, and restart without leaving the playfield.

coreCapabilities.description: Accelerate hard, brake or reverse, steer, handbrake, drift, collide with visible barriers, and recover explicitly.
Run a grandstand intro, countdown, deterministic opponents, lap order, finish celebration, pause, and restart.
Render a wide technical track with procedural trees, race fixtures, a grandstand, and twenty animated character spectators.
Use automatic close drone shots of the crowd before and after racing, a speed-reactive quasi-isometric follow camera, or a complete circuit map without resetting play.
Reproject the same live world through any public drawing medium, with Oil selected initially.
Expose renderer retry and explicit vehicle respawn without hidden physics corrections.

acceptanceCriteria: The race surface dominates wide and narrow viewports; settings never read as the primary product.
The player reaches materially higher speed and can sustain a scored drift through steering or the handbrake.
Every gameplay collision corresponds to visible authored geometry and no force silently drags the player to the centre line.
The world contains deterministic procedural trees and character spectators rendered by the shared Doodle scene pass.
Automatic opening and finish cinematics frame recognisable animated character faces at close range before pulling back to the grid or circuit.
Keyboard, touch, and standard gamepad feed the same abstract actions; controller focus is visible and hints follow the most recently active device.
Pause, vehicle configuration, and renderer recovery are focus-contained surfaces operable without a pointer.
The layout remains operable at 320 CSS pixels and preserves an accessible textual race summary.
outOfScope: Network multiplayer, persistent leaderboards, track editing, competitive vehicle upgrades, and simulation-grade tyre modelling.

assetInventory.usageConstraint: Use the live-text Paper Circuit name without inventing a brand mark.
Use provider-loaded Barlow Condensed for arcade display and IBM Plex Mono for telemetry with system fallbacks.
The track, racers, trees, fixtures, grandstand, and spectators are live procedural geometry, never shipped illustrative stand-ins.

typography.family: Barlow Condensed and IBM Plex Mono
typography.loading: Load Barlow Condensed 800/800 italic and IBM Plex Mono 400/600 from the same Google Fonts provider pattern already used by the experiments, with explicit system fallbacks.
roles: Barlow Condensed for the game title, position, speed, countdown, and drift calls
IBM Plex Mono for controls, running order, lap, time, settings, and live status
typography.density: Oversized 29–68 px arcade events, compact 8–13 px telemetry, and 44–108 px coarse-pointer drive targets.

references.instruction: Retain bone paper, charcoal ink, oxide accents, oxidized green, technical monospace, and registration-line character; ignore its workbench composition and quiet instrument pacing.

Govern the 1440 by 900 full-field composition, angular edge HUD, technical track gesture, scenery distribution, crowd silhouette, drift callout, and large speed gauge. Live procedural output replaces the structural world gesture.
Govern the 390 by 844 full-height playfield, terse top HUD, bottom-corner speed and drift, and large overlapping touch cluster rather than stacking dashboard panels below the world.
Govern wide region allocation, overlay anchors, track-and-scenery distribution, and usable playfield space; visual finish remains governed by the corresponding target mock.
Govern narrow full-height field allocation, compact top controls, telemetry anchors, and touch-control footprint; visual finish remains governed by the corresponding target mock.

traits.instruction: The live world is the background and primary surface at every viewport; opaque UI exists only in clipped edge plates and never forms a page header, sidebar, or card grid.
The wide course visibly changes direction and hazard rhythm; trees and a twenty-character grandstand frame the action without hiding the racing line.
Speed, slip, drift chain, collision, and countdown appear as strong arcade events with non-colour text cues and immediate motion response.
Pair luminous procedural paper and imperfect pigment with angular near-black plates, oxide danger accents, and no glossy generic game chrome.
On narrow coarse pointers, five large drive targets overlay the lower field while telemetry compresses to essentials; the page does not become a vertical settings form.

content.provenance: User requirements and repository-backed vehicle, character, tree, medium, motion, and runtime contracts; racer names are local fictional fixture labels.
useCases: Complete a fast three-lap drift race
Change medium or camera during play
permissions: anonymous local player may operate every control
errorAndFreshness: All state is local and current; renderer failure preserves settings and exposes Retry; leaving the world triggers an announced explicit respawn.

representativeBecause.realTask: Oil race seed 4115 covers crowd intro, countdown, high-speed driving, drifting, visible collision, lap progression, finish, and crowd celebration against three opponents.
representativeBecause.typicalAndDense: Four racers, multiple tree instances, race fixtures, and a twenty-character crowd exercise a materially populated shared Doodle scene.
representativeBecause.adverseState: Off-road grip, impact, explicit respawn, pause, and recoverable WebGL startup failure are represented without hidden correction.
representativeBecause.coreCapabilitiesWork: Every declared arcade, race, world, camera, medium, and recovery capability connects to live state or a live control.

structureConstraints: Keep the procedural world full-bleed and reserve no desktop sidebar or document footer.
Keep position and lap at the upper-left edge, settings at the upper-right edge, drift at the lower centre, and speed at the lower-right edge.
Keep every overlay clear of the player's expected follow-camera focus region.
Keep the canvas full-height and compact medium plus pause into the top edge without introducing a settings section.
Use five at-least-44-pixel touch controls over the lower playfield and preserve keyboard equivalence.
Keep position, lap, speed, drift, and current order legible without covering the player focus region.

layers.instruction: Own live telemetry, native settings, controller-navigable modal surfaces, device-derived hints, error recovery, and status announcements over the field.
Own full-viewport containment, angular edge plates, responsive touch composition, focus, forced-colour, and reduced-motion behavior.
Own the live solid and inked-solid course, visible fixtures, vehicles, trees, grandstand, and character spectators; no static target artwork ships in the playfield.
